function: Configuration of passive RIS phase shifts (continuous and 1-, 2-, 4-bit discrete) that maximizes the wideband OFDM achievable rate, including UE mobility (p. 2-5, 9).
system: AP and UE with isotropic antennas (no arrays described), passive reflecting RIS with N=25-400 elements, wideband OFDM, fc=3 GHz, bandwidth up to 13.5 MHz (p. 2-3, 7-8, 10).
method: Custom MLP variant (5 layers, ReLU, Adam, lr 1e-2) trained unsupervised with loss equal to negative received power over subcarriers; soft-round for quantized phases (p. 4-5, 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulated wideband channel (Table I): LOS-dominated AP-RIS and RIS-UE paths, NLOS direct paths, Rice factors; 500 training and 1500 test samples (p. 2-3, 5, 7).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and testing (500 train, 1500 held-out samples); sweeps of bandwidth, RIS size, phase bits; UE random-walk mobility (p. 5, 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: alternating optimization with successive convex approximation and water-filling (AO), strongest tap maximization (STM), coherent-rate upper bound; learned baseline: none (p. 3-4, 6, 8).
metrics: Achievable rate (Mbit/s), relative rate to coherent bound (%), efficiency rate (share of RIS elements not reconfigured, %), asymptotic complexity (p. 6, 9).
complexity: Table III: AO O(K^3.5 N^4.5), NN O(KN^2 + K^2 N), STM O(MN); training cost excluded as offline (p. 6, 8).
openness: none: no code or data link; channel realizations are generated by the authors' own simulator (p. 6).
q1_support: p. 6: "the values and definitions ascribed to all fixed parameters of the channel model presented in Section II". Own simulator (uniform delays and angles, Rice factors, fc=3 GHz); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 6: "the same proportion of training and test samples used in Subsection III-C is applied for the numerical results shown throughout this section". Test samples are held out from the same simulator (p. 5); no model trained in one condition is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 12: "the proposed NN is far more efficient than the other methods, namely, the STM and AO". Both baselines are non-learned; no earlier learned RIS method or standard network (DQN, FCN, CNN) is compared.
q4_support: p. 6: "Table III then brings the global computational complexity of such methods"; Table III (p. 8) gives O(KN^2 + K^2 N) for the proposed NN.
q5_support: p. 6: "each training sample requires a new realization of the channel". Data come from the authors' own simulator; no link, DOI, public dataset or measured data is given.
notes: Included, area 3 (learned RIS phase-shift configuration). AP and UE have isotropic antennas (p. 6) but a RIS is present, so the single-antenna exclusion does not apply. Tables I to III (p. 7-8) are image-only and were read from the page images. In the mobility test (p. 11) departure angles are known only in training, but the mobility process is the same in training and testing, so q2 is 0.
